claim: At N=16, the accel_step margin first reached >= 0.1 at step 75 in seed 28 and at step 100 in seed 27. Seed 27 is no earlier than the step-100 crossing at N=64 (f-20261011-203659-4e2f). In both seeds val_mse_ratio was already below 1 by step 50 (0.225 and 0.232), before accel_step formed. Final accel_step R2 was 0.925 vs control 0.780 (seed 28) and 0.914 vs 0.764 (seed 27), margins 0.145-0.150 at layer 4. Force formed much later and stayed weaker: R2 0.624 vs 0.514 (seed 28, layer 4, formed at step 475) and 0.546 vs 0.413 (seed 27, layer 1, formed at step 350), margins 0.109-0.133. Distance reached margins of 0.69-0.74 by step 50.
confidence_note: The verdict follows the pre-registered rule: one seed (27) crossed at step 100. Both seeds also failed the second expected-if-true condition, because the model beat the constant-velocity baseline before accel_step crossed. The timing difference is small, though. Checkpoints are 25 steps apart, so 75 vs 100 is one checkpoint, and seed 28 did cross earlier than N=64. The N=64 reference comes from a different experiment with different seeds, not from a matched run here. Also, accel_step's control R2 is high (0.76-0.78), which leaves little room for margin, so when the margin crosses 0.1 depends heavily on the control. A matched N=16 vs N=64 vs N=256 comparison with shared seeds and denser early checkpoints (every 10 steps) could still show a small but consistent shift, which would turn this into a weak 'supported'. As things stand, coarser sampling does not clearly move formation earlier.
